subject: Request: multi-year term preservation exception + uplift cap for HelixPay
messages:
From: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@helixpay.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@helixpay.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Feb 2027 09:02:14 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft SOW + multi-year commercial questions

Rachel —

Thanks for sending the draft SOW. Before we loop legal we have two commercial asks from procurement that are going to be gating for our CFO:

1) Price preservation: they want a 36-month price-lock on token/unit rates in the SOW (no mid-term increases).
2) Renewal protection / uplift cap: if Redwood adjusts list pricing, they want an explicit uplift cap at 4% (compounded annually) for the first renewal after the multi-year term; anything above that and they have the right to terminate for convenience with 60 days notice.

HelixPay is committing to a 3.5MM ARR ramp and is willing to sign a 3-year committed capacity clause, but they need these protections baked into the contract.

Can Redwood accommodate? If not, what guardrails would you propose so we can keep the deal moving this month?

Attachments: HelixPay_SOW_v2.pdf

—Marco
VP, Finance
HelixPay

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Deal Desk <deal-desk@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Draft SOW + multi-year commercial questions

Team — forwarding HelixPay's ask. Summary: 3-year committed deal (~3.5MM ARR) but customer is pushing two non-standard items:

- 36-month absolute price lock (no increases mid-term)
- Renewal protection: uplift cap at 4% compounded annually at first renewal and termination right if exceeded

Why escalation: The price-lock reduces our ability to respond to increasing infra costs; uplift cap + termination is a revenue-protection risk. From sales perspective this is high value and strategic in payments vertical. They are willing to sign now if we can provide language.

Attachments: helixpay-pricing-model-yr3-projection.xlsx (token-level projection they sent).

Requested: I need an approval path / recommended counter-proposal we can present by EOD 2/9 so we don't lose CFO momentum. Key asks: whether we can offer a partial lock (year 1 firm, year 2-3 capped at X%), acceptable uplift cap range, and any required governance (e.g., cap tied to CPI or explicit exceptions for third-party GPU pricing shocks).

Thanks — Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Feb 2027 10:07:21 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Draft SOW + multi-year commercial questions

Quick thoughts from finance:

- Floor vs lock: absolute 36-month lock is high risk for us given volatility in GPU and cloud costs. We could accept a guaranteed effective-list-rate floor for year 1 and a predictable cap mechanism thereafter.
- Suggested structure: Year 1 fixed rates; Years 2–3 indexed cap where list increases are capped at max(annual CPI + 2%, 5%) — this protects HelixPay from outsized hikes while preserving upside for us if costs rise materially.
- Uplift cap at 4% compounded is reasonable only if we can: (a) reduce committed capacity SLAs (i.e., make autoscaling/burst optional), or (b) secure a higher minimum commitment (push some of the ARR to upfront or non-refundable credits).

If Sales can accept modest compromise on capacity terms (burst window, preemption) we can accommodate a 4% cap for the first renewal. Otherwise counter at 6% with the indexing mechanism above.

Also: run revenue recognition implications with accounting for a locked multi-year rate — legal may need to flag termination rights for revenue deferral.

—Ben
VP, Finance
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 14:31:05 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Draft SOW + multi-year commercial questions

Appreciate the fast turn. Exec recommendation and request to Legal for redline:

Recommendation (commercial):
- Offer: 36-month term with the following rate mechanics:
  * Year 1: fixed locked rates as quoted in the SOW.
  * Years 2–3: list-rate adjustments allowed but capped by the higher of (CPI + 2%) or 5% per year (compounded).
  * First renewal after the 3-yr term: uplift cap of 6% (compounded) unless HelixPay increases committed capacity by >=25% or prepays 6 months of committed spend.

Trade-offs we want in the contract:
- Carve-outs for extraordinary third-party cost drivers (e.g., sanctioned GPU supply events) — Redwood may pass through incremental costs with notice.
- If customer insists on the 4% uplift cap, require 6 months non-refundable credit or prepayment of year 2 (or equivalent revenue protection).
- No additional SLA loosenings unless Legal signs off.

Legal ask (@Markus): please prepare a redline that implements the above and includes: termination mechanics tied to uplift breach, 60-day cure period, audit rights for usage and billing, and an explicit carve-out for force majeure/third-party costs. Also confirm whether the revenue recognition team needs a specific clause to avoid revenue deferral risk.

If Legal and Finance can confirm, I authorize Rachel to present this counter to HelixPay. Goal: have a signed SOW with these terms by 2/18.

—Marissa
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Draft SOW + multi-year commercial questions

Thanks — legal can implement Marissa's framework with the following caveats/clarifications:

- Term/Price Lock language: we will draft a "price preservation" clause that guarantees rates for Year 1 and implements an "indexed cap" for Years 2–3 (CPI + 2% floor, 5% minimum cap). This avoids an absolute prohibition on adjustments while giving the customer predictability.
- Uplift cap & termination: we'll add the 60-day cure and a termination for convenience right if uplift in the first renewal exceeds the capped amount. However, termination will be limited to termination of the renewal option, not retroactive cancellation of the prior committed term.
- Carve-outs: include explicit carve-outs for third-party cost events (GPU supply, major cloud price shocks), and require Redwood to provide 30 days' notice and an impact summary.
- Billing/audit: add audit rights and a clause requiring prepayment or non-refundable credits if HelixPay insists on the lower 4% uplift cap (we'll quantify the revenue protection number in the redline).
- Accounting: cc revenue ops — we will include language to mitigate revenue deferral (e.g., no automatic termination for price increases within the capped band). Please confirm if Finance wants specific wording; otherwise we'll use standard language.

I will push a redline to the Drive link and share the DocuSign-ready SOW once Marissa confirms.

—Markus
Chief Counsel, Redwood Inference

> Attachment placeholders: HelixPay_SOW_v2.pdf, helixpay-pricing-model-yr3-projection.xlsx
